sn2.17:2.3: Reading kiccesu with the Thai version. The Burmese version has kicchesu, “troubles.”
sn2.17:3.1: Reading bojjhaṅga-tapasā with the Thai version. The Burmese version has bojjhā tapasā, “from awakening, from austerity.” The Commentary notes that bojjhaṅga/bojjhā refers to the development of the factors of awakening (see MN 118). Tapasā, it says, refers to undertaking the dhutaṅga practices (see Thag 16:7).
sn2.17:3.3: On the definition of the all, see SN 35:23.
